A {{height|ft=6|in=10}} tall [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]]/[[Center (basketball)|center]], he played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]] and played in one game for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Comanche was playing for the [[Stockton Kings]] of the [[NBA G League]] in 2023 when he and his ex-girlfriend, Sakari Harnden, were arrested and charged with the kidnap and murder of a 23-year-old woman. ==High school and college career== He attended [[View Park Preparatory High School]], before graduating from [[Beverly Hills High School]] in 2015, after having averaged 20.1 points, 16 rebounds and four blocks per game as a senior en route to a Southern Section 3A title. In his two years at the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|University of Arizona]] (2015–2017), Comanche saw the court in 60 games, producing averages of 4.9 points and 2.8 boards a contest. On April 8, 2017, he declared for the [[2017 NBA draft]]{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19112051/arizona-wildcats-sophomore-chance-comanche-declares-nba-draft|title=Zona sophomore Comanche to test NBA waters|work=ESPN.com|access-date=May 26, 2017}} and on May 5, 2017, announced his decision to forgo the remaining two years of his college eligibility and to stay in the draft.{{Cite news|url=http://www.wildcat.arizona.edu/article/2017/05/s-comanche-is-stupid|title=Chance Comanche won't return to Arizona, keeps name in draft|work=The Daily Wildcat|access-date=May 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190201013425/http://www.wildcat.arizona.edu/article/2017/05/s-comanche-is-stupid|archive-date=February 1, 2019|url-status=dead}} However, he was not selected by any team. ==Professional career== After going undrafted, Comanche joined the [[Drew League]], a pro-am league after not being invited to the [[NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|first=Ryan|last=Kelapire|title=Arizona basketball: Chance Comanche playing in the Drew League|url=https://www.azdesertswarm.com/basketball/2017/7/24/16016168/arizona-basketball-chance-comanche-playing-drew-league-nba-summer-league-europe-contract-sign-stats|website=AZDesertSwarm.com|date=July 24, 2017|access-date=July 24, 2017}} ===Memphis Hustle (2017–2018)=== On November 2, 2017, he joined the [[Memphis Hustle]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|first=Bruce|last=Pascoe|title=Ex-Cat Chance Comanche makes G League roster; Auburn benches 2 amid FBI probe|url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/ex-cat-chance-comanche-makes-g-league-roster-auburn-benches/article_23790a46-c00f-11e7-9c79-b79ee2142c4d.html|website=Tucson.com|date=November 2, 2017|access-date=November 2, 2017}} In his first season of play, he averaged 9.2 points and 5.4 rebounds per game for the Hustle.{{cite web|first=Ryan|last=Kelapire|title=Chance Comanche enjoying his time in the NBA G League|url=https://www.azdesertswarm.com/basketball/2018/2/6/16973222/chance-comanche-enjoying-nba-g-league-stats-memphis-hustle-arizona-wildcats-highlights|website=AZDesertSwarm.com|date=February 6, 2018|access-date=February 6, 2018}} He would not be on the Memphis Hustle's roster for the 2018–19 season. ===Canton Charge (2019)=== On January 7, 2019, the [[Canton Charge]] acquired Comanche from the [[Memphis Hustle]] for one of the [[Raptors 905]]'s 2019 second-round pick and the returning rights to [[Jordan Mathews]].{{cite web|title=Charge Trade For Chance Comanche|url=https://canton.gleague.nba.com/news/charge-trade-for-chance-comanche/|website=NBA.com|date=January 7, 2019|access-date=January 7, 2019|archive-date=January 8, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190108101008/https://canton.gleague.nba.com/news/charge-trade-for-chance-comanche/|url-status=dead}} Comanche would later play with the Canton Charge during the rest of the 2018–19 season. However, he would not play with the Charge during the 2019–20 season or the 2020–21 bubble shortened season. ===Enid Outlaws (2021)=== In 2021, Comanche signed with the [[Enid Outlaws]] of [[The Basketball League]]. On April 19, he scored 43 points in a 152–78 win against the [[Lewisville Leopards]].{{cite news|first=Tarik|last=Masri|title=Comanche scores 43 in 74-point blowout|url=https://www.enidnews.com/sports/comanche-scores-43-in-74-point-blowout/article_86c3bd3c-a15a-11eb-93a4-270f9fa50d71.html|work=[[Enid News & Eagle]]|date=April 19, 2021|access-date=June 21, 2021}} Comanche averaged 27.4 points, 12.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.3 blocks per game. ===Ankara DSİ S.K. (2021)=== On June 24, 2021, he signed with [[Ankara DSİ S.K.]] (Yeni Mamak Spor) of the [[Turkish Basketball First League]].{{cite web|first=Fersu|last=Yahyabeyoglu|title=Chance Comanche joins Mamak|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Turkey/news/690674/Chance-Comanche-joins-Mamak|website=EuroBasket.com|date=June 24, 2021|access-date=December 1, 2021}} On December 21, he was named the league's player of the week after posting 24 points and 16 rebounds in a win against [[Bornova Belediyespor]].{{cite web|title=Chance Comanche gets MVP of the Week award for Turkish TBL|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Turkey/news/722746/Chance-Comanche-gets-MVP-of-the-Week-award-for-Turkish-TBL|website=EuroBasket.com|date=December 21, 2021|access-date=December 21, 2021}} release Chance Comanche following arrest by FBI in Sacramento County |url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/nba/sacramento-kings/article283120423.html |website=The Sacramento Bee}} in connection with a disappearance of a woman in [[Las Vegas]] named Marayna Rodgers.{{Cite web |date=2023-12-17 |title=NBA G League player Chance Comanche arrested in connection to Marayna Rodgers' disappearance |url=https://nypost.com/2023/12/17/sports/nba-g-league-player-chance-comanche-arrested-in-connection-to-marayna-rodgers-disappearance/ |access-date=2023-12-17 |website=New York Post |language=en}} The disappearance was first reported on December 7, with Comanche later playing for the Stockton Kings that same night in a 103–99 loss to the [[Rip City Remix]] at the [[Chiles Center]].{{Cite web |title=STO @ RCR, 2023-12-07 |url=https://gleague.nba.com/game/sto-vs-rcr-2052300162 |access-date=2024-01-16 |website=The NBA G League |language=en}} However, the incident was considered to have been planned since December 4, with the Stockton Kings being around the Las Vegas area for a game against the [[NBA G League Ignite]] in [[Henderson, Nevada]] on December 5 as one of the select few games that season where the NBA G League Ignite would win before being dissolved at the end of their final season of existence.{{Cite web |last= |date=2023-12-20 |title=Gun, ghost, coffin emojis: How ex-NBA player Chance Comanche confessed to strangling woman in Vegas |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/story/2023-12-20/chance-comanche-admits-killing-woman-las-vegas-nba-g-league-kings-marayna-rodgers |access-date=2024-01-24 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |title=STO @ GLI, 2023-12-05 |url=https://gleague.nba.com/game/sto-vs-gli-2052300150 |access-date=2024-01-16 |website=The NBA G League |language=en}} ==Murder charge== Comanche was released by the [[Stockton Kings]] of the [[NBA G League]] on December 15, 2023, after his arrest on kidnapping charges by the [[FBI]] in connection with the disappearance of 23-year-old [[Lynnwood, Washington|Lynnwood]], [[Washington (state)|Washington]], native Marayna Rodgers. Rodgers had been reported missing in [[Las Vegas, Nevada]], on December 7. Comanche's former girlfriend, 19-year-old Sakari Harnden, whom he had dated the previous year, had been arrested two days before in Las Vegas on charges relating to Rodgers' disappearance.{{cite news |last1=Murphy |first1=Vanessa |title=NBA G-league player and girlfriend "execute murder plan," accused of killing woman in Las Vegas valley, police say |url=https://www.8newsnow.com/investigators/timeline-former-nba-player-girlfriend-accused-of-murder-in-las-vegas/ |access-date=2023-12-17 |publisher=8NewsNow.com |date=2023-12-17}}{{Cite web |title=Ex-NBA player allegedly admitted to fatally strangling woman in Las Vegas, court documents show |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2023/12/20/former-nba-player-allegedly-admitted-to-fatally-strangling-woman-in-las-vegas-court-documents-show/71993574007/ |access-date=2024-01-16 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US}} Rodgers' remains were found in the Nevada desert days after Comanche admitted to police that he had strangled Rodgers and disposed of her body; he also showed the police on a map where her remains were located. On January 2, 2024, it was announced that separate murder, kidnapping and conspiracy charges would be combined so that both Comanche and Harnden could be tried together.{{cite web |title=Ex-NBA G League player, ex-girlfriend to face murder charge |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39230694/ex-nba-g-league-player-ex-girlfriend-face-murder-charge |website=ESPN |access-date=March 8, 2024 |date=January 2, 2024}} Comanche's lawyer asked the Las Vegas court to declare him [[indigent]] due to his spending "all of his and his family's funds to hire [[counsel]]".{{Cite web |date=2024-02-25 |title=Lawyers asking Las Vegas court to declare former NBA G League player indigent |url=https://www.ktnv.com/news/crime/lawyers-asking-las-vegas-court-to-declare-former-nba-g-league-player-indigent |access-date=2024-05-23 |website=Channel 13 Las Vegas News KTNV |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Zalucki |first=Rachel |date=2024-02-27 |title=G League player accused of Las Vegas murder asks for help covering attorney costs |url=https://www.fox5vegas.com/2024/02/27/g-league-player-accused-las-vegas-murder-asks-help-covering-attorney-costs/ |access-date=2025-09-12 |website=[[Fox 5 Vegas]] |language=en}} It was reported on March 28 of that year that Nevada prosecutors would not seek the death penalty against Comanche if he was convicted.{{Cite web |date=2024-03-28 |title=Lawyer: Ex-G Leaguer won't face death penalty |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39827279/lawyer-chance-comanche-face-death-penalty-convicted |access-date=2024-05-23 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} On April 3, state authorities announced that Comanche's trial would begin on March 10, 2025, but the trial date has been continued several times, and it is now expected to take place in 2026.{{Cite web |date=2024-04-03 |title=Ex-G Leaguer's murder trial set for March 2025 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39867251/ex-g-leaguer-chance-comanc-murder-trial-set-march-2025 |access-date=2025-10-10 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Wright |first=Jarah |date=2025-04-11 |title=Former G League player's confession should be suppressed, attorney says
